# HTML [GitHub-shaped export and import]

`exportDOM` emits GitHub's exact footnote shape, and import reads that shape
back — plus GitHub's own rendered output. The one deliberate divergence is
about orphan notes, and it has an opt-out.

## Export

A cue exports as GitHub's superscript anchor, the notes as a labelled section:

```html
<sup><a href="#fn-id" id="fnref-id" data-footnote-ref>1</a></sup>

<section data-footnotes class="footnotes">
  <h2 id="footnote-label" class="sr-only">Footnotes</h2>
  <ol>
    <li id="fn-id">
      <p>
        The note.
        <a
          href="#fnref-id"
          data-footnote-backref
          aria-label="Back to reference 1"
          >↩</a
        >
      </p>
    </li>
  </ol>
</section>
```

The `footnote-label` heading is visually hidden — it names the section for a
screen reader without printing a heading. A note cited more than once gets one
backref per cue, and the repeat cues carry suffixed ids (`fnref-id-2`) so each
backref lands on its own cue (`↩`, `↩²`, …).

## Import

Import accepts this output and GitHub's `user-content-`-prefixed variant — the
prefix is a host's namespacing concern, so the importer reads both. Definitions
declared as ordinary list items are slotted onto the single section wherever the
source put them.

## Orphan notes

One difference from GitHub: a definition nothing refers to is still exported.
This HTML is a document format, not only a rendering, and an orphan note is
content someone wrote — dropping it on export would be silent data loss.

If your HTML _is_ a rendering rather than a document, opt into GitHub's behavior
and leave orphans out:

```ts twoslash
// @twoslash-cache: {"v":1,"hash":"8639e6b833e5bb05f0245f7bc6a2e32d3bb3ccbc11ead53f8e63ac5f833f1f6d","data":""}
import {configExtension} from 'lexical';
import {FootnoteExtension} from 'lexical-footnote';

const configured = configExtension(FootnoteExtension, {
  dropOrphansOnExport: true,
});
```

:::note
This affects HTML export only — markdown export keeps orphan definitions either
way, as GFM permits.
:::
